conceptZh: 兩隊大小不一的積木小隊想握手，一個太大一個太小，臨時湊出「木」和「目」，握手時中間亮起小愛心。
morph: a tall brick stack becomes 木 and a small stack becomes 目
creativeAngle: 尺寸差太多，只好互相借積木臨場湊出左右兩半。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a soft apricot wall with a mint floor; the glyph is solid cobalt 相, 木 on the left and 目 on the right. A giant red brick squad stands at left and a tiny yellow brick squad stands at right. The Traditional Chinese glyph 相 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the tiny squad tries to climb onto the giant squad to shake hands and slips off; the first 相 is spoken as the first tiny brick falls. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): they trade bricks: the giant squad lends two long bricks to make 木 while the tiny squad stacks a small box with a bar inside it to form 目; the second 相 is spoken as the last brick clicks. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): one giant brick and one tiny brick finally shake hands and a small gold heart glows between them; 相信 is spoken as the heart pulses once. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 相 is perfectly still and unobstructed; the heart bobs and the bricks sway side to side in a happy wobble; the glyph is still. Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「相、相、相信」 (ㄒㄧㄤ、ㄒㄧㄤ、ㄒㄧㄤ ㄒㄧㄣˋ). Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.6s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only brick clicks and a warm tiny chime, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.

conceptZh: 調皮小老鼠叼走拉布拉多警長的哨子，警長繞大圈追、滑過頭、飛身撲倒，撞散的藍木板跌成「木」，撞翻的藍窗框立成「目」，最後兩人同時指著對方，就是「互相」。
object: a stack of four cobalt wooden planks and a tall cobalt window frame with two crossbars, knocked over by a belly-flopping Labrador sheriff chasing a whistle-stealing mouse
morph: the sheriff's belly-flop slide scatters the four planks into 木 on the left (one upright, one crossbar, two slanted legs) and flips the window frame upright on the right as 目 (a tall box with two inner bars), settling into the standard form of 相
creativeAngle: 前一版是安靜的積木握手，這版改成全新的追逐鬧劇：小老鼠偷哨子、警長越追圈越大、滑過頭、飛身撲空，撞擊本身把木板撞成「木」、窗框撞成「目」。詞選「互相」，畫面上兩人同時互指對方，聽到的和看到的是同一件事，且「互」只有一個讀音。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second 2D cartoon comedy, locked frontal camera, no cuts. Setting: a flat pale-lemon wall and a soft cream floor, nothing else behind. Stage props: at left a neat stack of four cobalt-blue wooden planks, at right a tall cobalt-blue window frame lying on its side with two crossbars inside. Lead: an original tiny cheeky grey cartoon mouse with huge round pink-lined ears, a long whippy tail and a permanent grin. Rival: an original big friendly golden cartoon Labrador sheriff dog with a gold star badge and a silver whistle on a cord, all floppy ears and good intentions.

Moment one, want it (0.0-1.5s): the mouse zips in from the right, snatches the whistle right off the sheriff's neck, waggles it at him and sticks out its tongue. The sheriff's eyes go wide, he points a big paw at the mouse and winds up, back legs scrabbling. The first 相 is spoken at about 0.6s as the whistle is snatched.

Moment two, try and miss (1.5-3.0s): the mouse runs a tight little circle in the middle of the floor; the sheriff charges after it in a much bigger loop, skids straight past the mouse on all four paws with a squeak, trips over his own front feet and rolls into a ball, then pops up dizzy. The mouse runs an even bigger loop around him, dangling the whistle.

Moment three, the big crash (3.0-4.3s): the sheriff takes a flying leap at the mouse and belly-flops flat with a soft cartoon WHUMP; the mouse hops neatly over his head. His belly-slide plows into the plank stack: the four planks fly up with squash-and-stretch and drop into place as 木 on the left (one upright, one crossbar, two slanted legs), while his momentum bumps the window frame, which flips upright on the right as 目, a tall box with its two inner bars. The second 相 is spoken at about 3.9s as the last plank clicks down. The pieces settle precisely into the standard printed form of the Traditional Chinese glyph 相, 木 on the left and 目 on the right, in saturated cobalt blue, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with clear margins.

Moment four, payoff (4.3-5.0s): the mouse pops up at the bottom-left corner, the sheriff sits up at the bottom-right corner, and at the same instant they each point one finger straight at the other, looking at each other with matching surprised grins. The word 互相 is spoken at about 4.6s exactly as the two fingers point at each other.

Final hold (5.0-8.0s): the glyph 相 is perfectly still, fully visible and untouched. Below and beside it, small and away from the strokes, the mouse trots over and hands the whistle back, the sheriff gives one tiny proud toot and his tail wags, the mouse does a quick happy spin and bows. Nobody covers the glyph.

Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「相、相、互相」 (ㄒㄧㄤ、ㄒㄧㄤ、ㄏㄨˋ ㄒㄧㄤ). First utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 3.9s, the word at about 4.6s; then stop, no repeats, no other speech. Under the voice only soft cartoon pattering feet, a squeaky skid, a gentle whump, wood clacks and one tiny whistle toot, all quieter than the voice, no music. The single glyph 相 is the only text on screen; the vocabulary word is audio only, no subtitles, no watermark, no clutter, no flashing. Bright, clean colors, no neon, no white blowout, no dark grading.
